# UX Requirements Quality Checklist: Hero & About

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency, and testability of Feature 002's content and user experience requirements.
**Created**: 2026-11-02
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Content Authenticity and Positioning

- [x] CHK001 Does the specification distinguish the broad professional role in the headline from the short, verified focus phrase in the introduction, and say what to do when that phrase is unknown? [Clarity, Spec §Clarifications/FR-001/FR-002]
- [x] CHK002 Does it define required unverified values as neutral, accessible `Placeholder:` text and omit unavailable optional facts or destinations rather than displaying placeholders for them? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001/FR-005/FR-008/SC-006; Data Model §String-field placeholder contract]
- [x] CHK003 Are the prohibitions on fabricated employment, dates, qualifications, achievements, certifications, outcomes, and personal links applied consistently to both Hero and About content? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008/SC-003/SC-006; Constitution §Truthful content]
- [x] CHK004 Does FR-001 explicitly limit the verifiable-detail sentence rule to authored biography, exempt clearly marked placeholders, and define neutral placeholder wording while keeping authored copy concise, value-oriented, broad, and free of unsupported claims? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001/FR-002/FR-008/SC-001/SC-003/SC-006; Data Model §String-field placeholder contract]
- [x] CHK005 Does the typed content contract distinguish required editable fields from optional resume, social, and portrait data, including the omission behavior for absent values? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005/FR-008/FR-009; Plan §Content Model]

## Visual Hierarchy and About Scope

- [x] CHK006 Does the specification state the intended hero reading order among name, headline, introduction, required actions, optional supporting links, and optional portrait? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001/FR-003/FR-005/FR-009/FR-013]
- [x] CHK007 Does it define the relative prominence of the two required actions and ensure optional resume/social links remain subordinate? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003/FR-005/SC-008]
- [x] CHK008 Does it set a useful content-density boundary for the hero and specify that the first view should communicate identity, engineering focus, and next actions? [Measurability, Spec §FR-001/SC-001]
- [x] CHK009 Does About explicitly cover all six required subjects while limiting length to approximately 150 words and requiring a scannable presentation? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006/SC-003]
- [x] CHK010 Are the exclusions for detailed experience, education, certification, and skills catalogs clear enough to avoid duplicating Feature 004? [Scope, Spec §FR-007/FR-017/SC-003]
- [x] CHK011 Does the specification require one descriptive page H1, a subordinate About heading, and text-based access to meaningful content? [Accessibility, Spec §FR-011]

## Actions and Navigation Compatibility

- [x] CHK012 Are the exact required action labels and destinations defined, including View Projects → `#portfolio` and Contact Me → `#contact`? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003/SC-002]
- [x] CHK013 Does the specification define how each CTA behaves with JavaScript disabled and avoid making successful navigation depend on animation? [Progressive Enhancement, Spec §FR-014; Plan §Navigation behavior]
- [x] CHK014 Does it state that `#home` and `#about` remain the Home and About destinations and that Feature 001 remains the sole owner of `aria-current`, fragment/history synchronization, and active navigation styling? [Compatibility, Spec §FR-004; Plan §Navigation behavior]
- [x] CHK015 Are optional resume and social actions omitted when unavailable, and are their file/URL verification and lower-emphasis placement rules explicit? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-005/SC-006/SC-008]
- [x] CHK016 Do the acceptance criteria distinguish required CTA checks from optional-link checks, including the expected absent-data case? [Testability, Spec §SC-002/SC-006]

## Responsive Behavior and Visual Reference

- [x] CHK017 Are all supported widths—320, 375, 768, 1024, 1440, and 1920 CSS pixels—listed in the requirements and tied to observable outcomes? [Coverage, Spec §FR-013/SC-004]
- [x] CHK018 Does the specification define mobile content/action order before portrait media at 320–767px and give a readability condition for side-by-side layouts at 768px and above? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
- [x] CHK019 Do responsive acceptance criteria cover overflow, clipped headlines, overlap, accessible CTAs, portrait placement, and readable About content rather than merely saying “responsive”? [Measurability, Spec §FR-013/SC-004]
- [x] CHK020 Does the specification preserve Feature 001's dark canvas, blue accents, typography, spacing, content width, and action patterns while allowing hierarchy improvements? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010/SC-008; Plan §Design and Implementation Decisions]
- [x] CHK021 Does it accurately document the current screenshot availability limitation and prohibit inventing visual details from unavailable references? [Assumptions, Spec §Assumptions/FR-010]

## Accessibility and Motion

- [x] CHK022 Do requirements cover semantic structure, meaningful accessible names, keyboard and pointer activation, visible focus, contrast, and practical 44×44 CSS-pixel targets? [Coverage, Spec §FR-011/FR-012/SC-005; Constitution §Accessible, responsive experience]
- [x] CHK023 Are normal-text, large-text, and control/state contrast thresholds stated where relevant, with manual contrast and assistive-technology findings kept distinct from automated scan results? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [x] CHK024 Does the image requirement distinguish informative portraits needing meaningful alternative text from decorative imagery needing empty alternative text, including the existing decorative fallback? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-009/SC-006]
- [x] CHK025 Does the specification require content and actions to remain understandable without nonessential motion and state how `prefers-reduced-motion` affects that motion? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014/SC-010; Constitution §Accessible, responsive experience]
- [x] CHK026 Are 200% zoom, keyboard focus/order, and automated versus manual accessibility checks assigned to explicit acceptance criteria? [Testability, Spec §SC-004/SC-005; Plan §Validation Strategy]

## Performance and Verification Boundaries

- [x] CHK027 Does performance guidance identify the Feature 001 baseline and require comparable mobile and desktop test profiles before claiming preservation or improvement? [Traceability, Spec §FR-016/SC-009; Plan §Performance]
- [x] CHK028 Are Lighthouse date/version, device/profile, all four category scores, lab LCP/CLS, and field INP reporting rules specified, including “not yet measurable” when field data is insufficient? [Measurability, Spec §FR-016/SC-007/SC-009/SC-010; Constitution §Fast, production-ready delivery]
- [x] CHK029 Does the specification address optional-media dimensions, load/failure behavior, image transfer, and media-caused layout shift without requiring an absent portrait? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-009/FR-015/SC-006/SC-007]
- [x] CHK030 Are the performance thresholds and the “preserve or improve Feature 001” goal stated without treating the existing desktop score below 90 as an already-passed target? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016/SC-007/SC-009; Plan §Performance]
- [x] CHK031 Are every success criterion and user-visible requirement traceable to a specific observable review, automated test, or measurement, with qualitative visitor review explicitly non-gating? [Traceability, Spec §SC-001–SC-011; Constitution §Verifiable changes and acceptance]

## Post-Implementation Validation (Not Checklist Completion)

The questions above assess specification quality only. Checking them does not demonstrate that the implementation works or that any runtime acceptance criterion has passed. After implementation, use the Feature 002 validation plan and record observed results for rendered hierarchy and all supported widths; CTA fragments and Feature 001 navigation state/history; JavaScript-disabled behavior; missing, delayed, and failed optional media; keyboard and screen-reader access; contrast, axe, 200% zoom, and reduced motion; visual consistency review; hydration console output; and reproducible mobile/desktop Lighthouse measurements. Keep manual accessibility, visual review, and field INP outcomes unclaimed until actually measured.
